You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\\n\\n# Python Testing with pytest\\n\\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\\n\\n## Structure and naming\\n\\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\\n\\n## Fixtures over setUp\\n\\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\\n\\n```python\\nimport pytest\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef settings(tmp_path):\\n # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\\n return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \\\"test.db\\\"))\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef repo(settings):\\n conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\\n run_migrations(conn)\\n yield Repository(conn) # everything after yield is teardown\\n conn.close()\\n```\\n\\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\\n\\n## Parametrize instead of loops\\n\\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\\n\\n```python\\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\\n (\\\"title_a\\\", \\\"title_b\\\", \\\"expected\\\"),\\n [\\n (\\\"Song (Live)\\\", \\\"Song\\\", True),\\n (\\\"Song\\\", \\\"Totally Other\\\", False),\\n ],\\n ids=[\\\"live-suffix-matches\\\", \\\"different-titles-reject\\\"],\\n)\\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\\n assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\\n```\\n\\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\\n\\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\\n\\n```toml\\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\\nasyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"\\n```\\n\\n```python\\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\\n httpx_mock.add_response(json={\\\"items\\\": []})\\n result = await client.get_playlist(\\\"abc\\\")\\n assert result == []\\n```\\n\\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\\n\\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\\n\\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\\n\\n```python\\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\\n def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\\n monkeypatch.setattr(client, \\\"get_playlist\\\", boom)\\n # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\\n```\\n\\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\\n\\n## Coverage and CI\\n\\n```bash\\npytest # all tests\\npytest -k \\\"match and not slow\\\" # filter by name expression\\npytest -x --ff # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match # one test\\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing # coverage with missing lines\\n```\\n\\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` or mark it. |\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn't awaitable. |\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. Default to `function` scope. |\n| Loop over cases in one test | Use `parametrize` so each case runs and reports independently. |\n| Mocking your own pure logic | Mock only I/O boundaries; test real logic directly. |\n| Shared session/file DB across tests | Give each test its own DB via `tmp_path` (function scope); a shared file leaks state and throws `database is locked` under parallel workers. |\n| `assertEqual`/`TestCase` boilerplate | Use plain `assert`; pytest rewrites it with rich diffs. |\n\n## References\n\n- [pytest documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [pytest-asyncio](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/)\n- [pytest-httpx](https://github.com/Colin-b/pytest_httpx)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"

        "<skill_content name=\"python-testing\">\n# Skill: python-testing\n\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\n\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\n\n# Python Testing with pytest\n\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\n\n## Structure and naming\n\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\n\n## Fixtures over setUp\n\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef settings(tmp_path):\n # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\n return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \"test.db\"))\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef repo(settings):\n conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\n run_migrations(conn)\n yield Repository(conn) # everything after yield is teardown\n conn.close()\n```\n\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\n\n## Parametrize instead of loops\n\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\n\n```python\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n (\"title_a\", \"title_b\", \"expected\"),\n [\n (\"Song (Live)\", \"Song\", True),\n (\"Song\", \"Totally Other\", False),\n ],\n ids=[\"live-suffix-matches\", \"different-titles-reject\"],\n)\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\n assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\n```\n\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\n\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\n\n```toml\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\nasyncio_mode = \"auto\"\n```\n\n```python\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\n httpx_mock.add_response(json={\"items\": []})\n result = await client.get_playlist(\"abc\")\n assert result == []\n```\n\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\n\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\n\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\n\n```python\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\n def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\n monkeypatch.setattr(client, \"get_playlist\", boom)\n # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\n```\n\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\n\n## Coverage and CI\n\n```bash\npytest # all tests\npytest -k \"match and not slow\" # filter by name expression\npytest -x --ff # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match # one test\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing # coverage with missing lines\n```\n\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\n\n## Targeted mutation testing\n\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\n\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\n\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\n\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\n\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` or mark it. |\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn't awaitable. |\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. Default to `function` scope. |\n| Loop over cases in one test | Use `parametrize` so each case runs and reports independently. |\n| Mocking your own pure logic | Mock only I/O boundaries; test real logic directly. |\n| Shared session/file DB across tests | Give each test its own DB via `tmp_path` (function scope); a shared file leaks state and throws `database is locked` under parallel workers. |\n| `assertEqual`/`TestCase` boilerplate | Use plain `assert`; pytest rewrites it with rich diffs. |\n\n## References\n\n- [pytest documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [pytest-asyncio](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/)\n- [pytest-httpx](https://github.com/Colin-b/pytest_httpx)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"

      "{\"type\":\"step_start\",\"timestamp\":1793301234862,\"sessionID\":\"ses_e76eabcc9ffeoa5IK0JPqR2117\",\"part\":{\"id\":\"prt_1891544ae001IDWDlvXO9d8fBh\",\"sessionID\":\"ses_e76eabcc9ffeoa5IK0JPqR2117\",\"messageID\":\"msg_1891544880011NjIpdmNK6n3rM\",\"type\":\"step-start\"}}\n{\"type\":\"tool_use\",\"timestamp\":1793301234881,\"sessionID\":\"ses_e76eabcc9ffeoa5IK0JPqR2117\",\"part\":{\"partID\":\"prt_1891544b1001MuQRbQOZWf2o98\",\"sessionID\":\"ses_e76eabcc9ffeoa5IK0JPqR2117\",\"messageID\":\"msg_1891544880011NjIpdmNK6n3rM\",\"type\":\"tool\",\"id\":\"fixture-skill-call\",\"tool\":\"skill\",\"state\":{\"status\":\"completed\",\"input\":{\"id\":\"python-testing\"},\"output\":\"<skill_content name=\\\"python-testing\\\">\\n# Skill: python-testing\\n\\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\\n\\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\\n\\n# Python Testing with pytest\\n\\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\\n\\n## Structure and naming\\n\\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\\n\\n## Fixtures over setUp\\n\\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\\n\\n```python\\nimport pytest\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef settings(tmp_path):\\n # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\\n return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \\\"test.db\\\"))\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef repo(settings):\\n conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\\n run_migrations(conn)\\n yield Repository(conn) # everything after yield is teardown\\n conn.close()\\n```\\n\\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\\n\\n## Parametrize instead of loops\\n\\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\\n\\n```python\\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\\n (\\\"title_a\\\", \\\"title_b\\\", \\\"expected\\\"),\\n [\\n (\\\"Song (Live)\\\", \\\"Song\\\", True),\\n (\\\"Song\\\", \\\"Totally Other\\\", False),\\n ],\\n ids=[\\\"live-suffix-matches\\\", \\\"different-titles-reject\\\"],\\n)\\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\\n assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\\n```\\n\\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\\n\\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\\n\\n```toml\\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\\nasyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"\\n```\\n\\n```python\\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\\n httpx_mock.add_response(json={\\\"items\\\": []})\\n result = await client.get_playlist(\\\"abc\\\")\\n assert result == []\\n```\\n\\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\\n\\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\\n\\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\\n\\n```python\\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\\n def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\\n monkeypatch.setattr(client, \\\"get_playlist\\\", boom)\\n # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\\n```\\n\\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\\n\\n## Coverage and CI\\n\\n```bash\\npytest # all tests\\npytest -k \\\"match and not slow\\\" # filter by name expression\\npytest -x --ff # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match # one test\\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing # coverage with missing lines\\n```\\n\\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\\n\\n## Targeted mutation testing\\n\\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\\n\\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\\n\\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\\n\\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\\n\\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\\n\\n## Common mistakes\\n\\n| Mistake | Fix |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors. Set `asyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"` or mark it. |\\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn't awaitable. |\\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. Default to `function` scope. |\\n| Loop over cases in one test | Use `parametrize` so each case runs and reports independently. |\\n| Mocking your own pure logic | Mock only I/O boundaries; test real logic directly. |\\n| Shared session/file DB across tests | Give each test its own DB via `tmp_path` (function scope); a shared file leaks state and throws `database is locked` under parallel workers. |\\n| `assertEqual`/`TestCase` boilerplate | Use plain `assert`; pytest rewrites it with rich diffs. |\\n\\n## References\\n\\n- [pytest documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\\n- [pytest-asyncio](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/)\\n- [pytest-httpx](https://github.com/Colin-b/pytest_httpx)\\n\\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\\nNote: file list is sampled.\\n\\n<skill_files>\\n</skill_files>\\n</skill_content>\",\"title\":\"skill\",\"metadata\":{\"metadata\":{\"name\":\"python-testing\",\"directory\":\"/workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\",\"truncated\":false},\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"<skill_content name=\\\"python-testing\\\">\\n# Skill: python-testing\\n\\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\\n\\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\\n\\n# Python Testing with pytest\\n\\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\\n\\n## Structure and naming\\n\\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\\n\\n## Fixtures over setUp\\n\\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\\n\\n```python\\nimport pytest\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef settings(tmp_path):\\n # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\\n return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \\\"test.db\\\"))\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef repo(settings):\\n conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\\n run_migrations(conn)\\n yield Repository(conn) # everything after yield is teardown\\n conn.close()\\n```\\n\\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\\n\\n## Parametrize instead of loops\\n\\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\\n\\n```python\\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\\n (\\\"title_a\\\", \\\"title_b\\\", \\\"expected\\\"),\\n [\\n (\\\"Song (Live)\\\", \\\"Song\\\", True),\\n (\\\"Song\\\", \\\"Totally Other\\\", False),\\n ],\\n ids=[\\\"live-suffix-matches\\\", \\\"different-titles-reject\\\"],\\n)\\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\\n assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\\n```\\n\\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\\n\\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\\n\\n```toml\\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\\nasyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"\\n```\\n\\n```python\\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\\n httpx_mock.add_response(json={\\\"items\\\": []})\\n result = await client.get_playlist(\\\"abc\\\")\\n assert result == []\\n```\\n\\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\\n\\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\\n\\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\\n\\n```python\\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\\n def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\\n monkeypatch.setattr(client, \\\"get_playlist\\\", boom)\\n # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\\n```\\n\\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\\n\\n## Coverage and CI\\n\\n```bash\\npytest # all tests\\npytest -k \\\"match and not slow\\\" # filter by name expression\\npytest -x --ff # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match # one test\\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing # coverage with missing lines\\n```\\n\\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\\n\\n## Targeted mutation testing\\n\\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\\n\\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\\n\\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\\n\\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption.           "<skill_content name=\"python-testing\">\n# Skill: python-testing\n\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\n\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\n\n# Python Testing with pytest\n\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\n\n## Structure and naming\n\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\n\n## Fixtures over setUp\n\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef settings(tmp_path):\n # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\n return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \"test.db\"))\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef repo(settings):\n conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\n run_migrations(conn)\n yield Repository(conn) # everything after yield is teardown\n conn.close()\n```\n\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\n\n## Parametrize instead of loops\n\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\n\n```python\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n (\"title_a\", \"title_b\", \"expected\"),\n [\n (\"Song (Live)\", \"Song\", True),\n (\"Song\", \"Totally Other\", False),\n ],\n ids=[\"live-suffix-matches\", \"different-titles-reject\"],\n)\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\n assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\n```\n\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\n\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.         "<skill_content name=\"python-testing\">\n# Skill: python-testing\n\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\n\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\n\n# Python Testing with pytest\n\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\n\n## Structure and naming\n\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\n\n## Fixtures over setUp\n\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef settings(tmp_path):\n # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\n return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \"test.db\"))\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef repo(settings):\n conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\n run_migrations(conn)\n yield Repository(conn) # everything after yield is teardown\n conn.close()\n```\n\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\n\n## Parametrize instead of loops\n\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\n\n```python\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n (\"title_a\", \"title_b\", \"expected\"),\n [\n (\"Song (Live)\", \"Song\", True),\n (\"Song\", \"Totally Other\", False),\n ],\n ids=[\"live-suffix-matches\", \"different-titles-reject\"],\n)\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\n assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\n```\n\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\n\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\n\n```toml\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\nasyncio_mode = \"auto\"\n```\n\n```python\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\n httpx_mock.add_response(json={\"items\": []})\n result = await client.get_playlist(\"abc\")\n assert result == []\n```\n\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\n\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\n\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\n\n```python\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\n def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\n monkeypatch.setattr(client, \"get_playlist\", boom)\n # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\n```\n\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\n\n## Coverage and CI\n\n```bash\npytest # all tests\npytest -k \"match and not slow\" # filter by name expression\npytest -x --ff # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match # one test\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing # coverage with missing lines\n```\n\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\n\n## Targeted mutation testing\n\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\n\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\n\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\n\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\n\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` or mark it. |\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn't awaitable. |\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. Default to `function` scope. |\n| Loop over cases in one test | Use `parametrize` so each case runs and reports independently. |\n| Mocking your own pure logic | Mock only I/O boundaries; test real logic directly. |\n| Shared session/file DB across tests | Give each test its own DB via `tmp_path` (function scope); a shared file leaks state and throws `database is locked` under parallel workers. |\n| `assertEqual`/`TestCase` boilerplate | Use plain `assert`; pytest rewrites it with rich diffs. |\n\n## References\n\n- [pytest documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [pytest-asyncio](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/)\n- [pytest-httpx](https://github.com/Colin-b/pytest_httpx)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"

name=\\"python-error-handling\\">\\n# Skill: python-error-handling\\n\\n> Pair with `python-common-practice`, `python-fastapi` (HTTP mapping), `python-async` (CancelledError), and `python-observability` (logging errors) as relevant.\\n\\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats exceptions as part of the API. You catch what you can handle and let the rest propagate to someone who can.\\n\\n# Error Handling\\n\\nPython prefers **EAFP** (\\"easier to ask forgiveness than permission\\") — try the operation and handle the exception rather than pre-checking. Pre-checks race with reality; the exception is the truth.\\n\\n```python\\n# ✓ EAFP — one atomic attempt\\ntry:\\n return cache[key]\\nexcept KeyError:\\n return load(key)\\n\\n# ✗ LBYL — racy for I/O; fine when a simple guard avoids broad catching\\nif key in cache:\\n return cache[key]\\n```\\n\\n**EAFP is a convention, not a universal rule.** Broad catches can hide failures from both humans and agents. Prefer EAFP where the exception type is known and the catch is narrow; inspect the framework\'s actual error behavior rather than guessing at its hierarchy. Use explicit checks where they express the contract more clearly, while accounting for race conditions between checking and acting.\\n\\n## Catch narrowly\\n\\nCatch the **specific** exception you can handle. A bare `except:` or `except Exception:` swallows bugs, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and (in async) cancellation — turning a crash you\'d fix into silent wrong behavior.\\n\\n```python\\n# ✗ Bad — hides programming errors and makes debugging impossible\\ntry:\\n sync_playlist(p)\\nexcept Exception:\\n pass\\n\\n# ✓ Good — handle the failures you expect; let the rest surface\\ntry:\\n sync_playlist(p)\\nexcept (httpx.HTTPError, TimeoutError) as e:\\n log.warning(\\"sync failed for %s: %s\\", p.id, e)\\n metrics.errors_total.inc()\\n```\\n\\nIf you must catch broadly (a top-level worker loop that must not die), log with `log.exception(...)` to capture the traceback, then continue or re-raise — never `pass`.\\n\\n## Agent navigability — narrow exception surfaces\\n\\nPrefer narrow exception surfaces: agents catching from broad hierarchies must guess error object shapes — a predictable interface failure, not a model failure.\\n\\n**Framework guidance — catch the specific exception, not the family:**\\n\\n| Framework | Broad (avoid) | Narrow (prefer) |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| `requests` / `httpx` | `requests.exceptions.RequestException` | `httpx.TimeoutException`, `httpx.HTTPStatusError` |\\n| `django` ORM | `django.core.exceptions.ObjectDoesNotExist` | `MyModel.DoesNotExist` |\\n| SQLAlchemy | `sqlalchemy.exc.SQLAlchemyError` | `sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError`, `sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError` |\\n\\nWrap framework exceptions at the boundary into domain exceptions. This collapses the broad hierarchy into a predictable, narrow surface for all downstream code.\\n\\n## Custom exceptions — a hierarchy with a common base\\n\\nGive your package one base exception; specific errors subclass it. Callers can then catch the whole family or a specific case. This is what lets a FastAPI handler map *all* your domain errors in one place.\\n\\n```python\\nclass SortarrError(Exception):\\n \\"\\"\\"Base for all sortarr domain errors.\\"\\"\\"\\n\\nclass AuthRequiredError(SortarrError): ...\\nclass QuotaExceededError(SortarrError): ...\\n```\\n\\nSubclass the most specific stdlib type when it fits (`ValueError`, `LookupError`); invent a new hierarchy only for domain concepts the stdlib doesn\'t model.\\n\\n## Chain exceptions — preserve the cause\\n\\nWhen you wrap a low-level error in a domain one, use `raise ... from` so the original traceback survives. Bare `raise NewError(...)` inside an `except` hides the root cause.\\n\\n```python\\ntry:\\n resp = await client.get(url)\\n resp.raise_for_status()\\nexcept httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:\\n raise QuotaExceededError(\\"YouTube quota hit\\") from e # ✓ keeps the cause\\n```\\n\\nTo deliberately suppress the context, use `from None` — and only when the cause is genuinely noise.\\n\\nThis is also how you keep storage details out of the API: the **repository** catches the driver error and raises a domain error, so the route never imports `sqlite3` or sees a driver exception.\\n\\n```python\\nimport sqlite3\\n\\ndef save_rule(self, rule: Rule) -> None:\\n try:\\n self._con.execute(\\"INSERT INTO rules (id, pattern) VALUES (?, ?)\\", (rule.id, rule.pattern))\\n except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:\\n raise DuplicateRuleError(rule.id) from e # domain error — a handler maps it to 409\\n```\\n\\n## else and finally\\n\\n`else` runs only when `try` didn\'t raise — put success logic there. `finally` always runs; prefer a **context manager** over manual try/finally.\\n\\n```python\\nwith open_connection(db_path) as conn: # closed on any exit path\\n conn.execute(...)\\n```\\n\\nWrite your own with `contextlib.contextmanager` or `__enter__/__exit__`; use `async with` for async resources.\\n\\n## Re-raise, don\'t return error sentinels\\n\\nReturning `None`/`-1`/`False` to signal failure forces every caller to remember to check, and the type checker can\'t help. Raise instead — the failure can\'t be silently ignored. (Return `X | None` only when \\"not found\\" is a *normal, expected* outcome, not an error.)\\n\\nIn async code, **never swallow `asyncio.CancelledError`** — re-raise it so shutdown and timeouts work (→ See `python-async`).\\n\\n## Mapping to HTTP\\n\\nIn FastAPI, register one exception handler per domain base class rather than try/except in every route (→ See `python-fastapi`):\\n\\n```python\\n@app.exception_handler(AuthRequiredError)\\nasync def _auth(_: Request, exc: AuthRequiredError):\\n return JSONResponse(status_code=401, content={\\"detail\\": str(exc)})\\n```\\n\\nNever leak a stack trace or internal message to a client — log the detail server-side, return a clean message.\\n\\n## Common mistakes\\n\\n| Mistake | Fix |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `except Exception: pass` | Catch the specific type; if broad, `log.exception` then re-raise. |\\n| Bare `raise FooError()` inside `except` | `raise FooError() from err` to preserve the cause. |\\n| `except:` (bare) | Catches `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`/cancellation too — name the type. |\\n| Manual try/finally for cleanup | Use a context manager (`with`). |\\n| Returning `None`/`-1` for errors | Raise an exception; reserve `None` for expected absence. |\\n| Swallowing `CancelledError` in async | Re-raise it. |\\n| Leaking tracebacks to API clients | Log server-side; return a sanitized message. |\\n| EAFP with broad `except` on a framework hierarchy | Prefer LBYL guard or narrow catch; wrap at the boundary into a domain exception. |\\n\\n**Diagnose:** 1- `ruff check` (bugbear `B`) — flags overly broad `except` and `raise` without `from` 2- read the full traceback (don\'t truncate) — the chained `from` cause usually names the real failure.\\n\\n## References\\n\\n- [Errors and Exceptions — tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html)\\n- [Built-in Exceptions](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html)\\n- [Glossary — EAFP / LBYL](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html)\\n- [Alexis King — Parse, don\'t validate](https://lexi-lambda.github.io/blog/2019/11/05/parse-don-t-validate/)\\n\\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-error-handling\\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\\nNote: file list is sampled.\\n\\n<skill_files>\\n</skill_files>\\n</skill_content>","title":"skill","metadata":{"metadata":{"name":"python-error-handling","directory":"/workspace/.opencode/skills/python-error-handling","truncated":false},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"<skill_content name=\\"python-error-handling\\">\\n# Skill: python-error-handling\\n\\n> Pair with `python-common-practice`, `python-fastapi` (HTTP mapping), `python-async` (CancelledError), and `python-observability` (logging errors) as relevant.\\n\\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats exceptions as part of the API. Bare `raise NewError(...)` inside an `except` hides the root cause.\n\n```python\ntry:\n resp = await client.get(url)\n resp.raise_for_status()\nexcept httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:\n raise QuotaExceededError("YouTube quota hit") from e # ✓ keeps the cause\n```\n\nTo deliberately suppress the context, use `from None` — and only when the cause is genuinely noise.\n\nThis is also how you keep storage details out of the API: the **repository** catches the driver error and raises a domain error, so the route never imports `sqlite3` or sees a driver exception.\n\n```python\nimport sqlite3\n\ndef save_rule(self, rule: Rule) -> None:\n try:\n self._con.execute("INSERT INTO rules (id, pattern) VALUES (?, ?)", (rule.id, rule.pattern))\n except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:\n raise DuplicateRuleError(rule.id) from e # domain error — a handler maps it to 409\n```\n\n## else and finally\n\n`else` runs only when `try` didn\'t raise — put success logic there. `finally` always runs; prefer a **context manager** over manual try/finally.\n\n```python\nwith open_connection(db_path) as conn: # closed on any exit path\n conn.execute(...)\n```\n\nWrite your own with `contextlib.contextmanager` or `__enter__/__exit__`; use `async with` for async resources.\n\n## Re-raise, don\'t return error sentinels\n\nReturning `None`/`-1`/`False` to signal failure forces every caller to remember to check, and the type checker can\'t help. Raise instead — the failure can\'t be silently ignored. (Return `X | None` only when "not found" is a *normal, expected* outcome, not an error.)\n\nIn async code, **never swallow `asyncio.CancelledError`** — re-raise it so shutdown and timeouts work (→ See `python-async`).\n\n## Mapping to HTTP\n\nIn FastAPI, register one exception handler per domain base class rather than try/except in every route (→ See `python-fastapi`):\n\n```python\n@app.exception_handler(AuthRequiredError)\nasync def _auth(_: Request, exc: AuthRequiredError):\n return JSONResponse(status_code=401, content={"detail": str(exc)})\n```\n\nNever leak a stack trace or internal message to a client — log the detail server-side, return a clean message.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `except Exception: pass` | Catch the specific type; if broad, `log.exception` then re-raise. |\n| Bare `raise FooError()` inside `except` | `raise FooError() from err` to preserve the cause. |\n| `except:` (bare) | Catches `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`/cancellation too — name the type. |\n| Manual try/finally for cleanup | Use a context manager (`with`). |\n| Returning `None`/`-1` for errors | Raise an exception; reserve `None` for expected absence. |\n| Swallowing `CancelledError` in async | Re-raise it. |\n| Leaking tracebacks to API clients | Log server-side; return a sanitized message. |\n| EAFP with broad `except` on a framework hierarchy | Prefer LBYL guard or narrow catch; wrap at the boundary into a domain exception. |\n\n**Diagnose:** 1- `ruff check` (bugbear `B`) — flags overly broad `except` and `raise` without `from` 2- read the full traceback (don\'t truncate) — the chained `from` cause usually names the real failure.\n\n## References\n\n- [Errors and Exceptions — tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html)\n- [Built-in Exceptions](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html)\n- [Glossary — EAFP / LBYL](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html)\n- [Alexis King — Parse, don\'t validate](https://lexi-lambda.github.io/blog/2019/11/05/parse-don-t-validate/)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-error-handling\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is You catch what you can handle and let the rest propagate to someone who can.\\n\\n# Error Handling\\n\\nPython prefers **EAFP** (\\\"easier to ask forgiveness than permission\\\") — try the operation and handle the exception rather than pre-checking. Pre-checks race with reality; the exception is the truth.\\n\\n```python\\n# ✓ EAFP — one atomic attempt\\ntry:\\n return cache[key]\\nexcept KeyError:\\n return load(key)\\n\\n# ✗ LBYL — racy for I/O; fine when a simple guard avoids broad catching\\nif key in cache:\\n return cache[key]\\n```\\n\\n**EAFP is a convention, not a universal rule.** Broad catches can hide failures from both humans and agents. Prefer EAFP where the exception type is known and the catch is narrow; inspect the framework's actual error behavior rather than guessing at its hierarchy. Use explicit checks where they express the contract more clearly, while accounting for race conditions between checking and acting.\\n\\n## Catch narrowly\\n\\nCatch the **specific** exception you can handle. A bare `except:` or `except Exception:` swallows bugs, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and (in async) cancellation — turning a crash you'd fix into silent wrong behavior.\\n\\n```python\\n# ✗ Bad — hides programming errors and makes debugging impossible\\ntry:\\n sync_playlist(p)\\nexcept Exception:\\n pass\\n\\n# ✓ Good — handle the failures you expect; let the rest surface\\ntry:\\n sync_playlist(p)\\nexcept (httpx.HTTPError, TimeoutError) as e:\\n log.warning(\\\"sync failed for %s: %s\\\", p.id, e)\\n metrics.errors_total.inc()\\n```\\n\\nIf you must catch broadly (a top-level worker loop that must not die), log with `log.exception(...)` to capture the traceback, then continue or re-raise — never `pass`.\\n\\n## Agent navigability — narrow exception surfaces\\n\\nPrefer narrow exception surfaces: agents catching from broad hierarchies must guess error object shapes — a predictable interface failure, not a model failure.\\n\\n**Framework guidance — catch the specific exception, not the family:**\\n\\n| Framework | Broad (avoid) | Narrow (prefer) |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| `requests` / `httpx` | `requests.exceptions.RequestException` | `httpx.TimeoutException`, `httpx.HTTPStatusError` |\\n| `django` ORM | `django.core.exceptions.ObjectDoesNotExist` | `MyModel.DoesNotExist` |\\n| SQLAlchemy | `sqlalchemy.exc.SQLAlchemyError` | `sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError`, `sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError` |\\n\\nWrap framework exceptions at the boundary into domain exceptions. This collapses the broad hierarchy into a predictable, narrow surface for all downstream code.\\n\\n## Custom exceptions — a hierarchy with a common base\\n\\nGive your package one base exception; specific errors subclass it. Callers can then catch the whole family or a specific case. This is what lets a FastAPI handler map *all* your domain errors in one place.\\n\\n```python\\nclass SortarrError(Exception):\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Base for all sortarr domain errors.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nclass AuthRequiredError(SortarrError): ...\\nclass QuotaExceededError(SortarrError): ...\\n```\\n\\nSubclass the most specific stdlib type when it fits (`ValueError`, `LookupError`); invent a new hierarchy only for domain concepts the stdlib doesn't model.\\n\\n## Chain exceptions — preserve the cause\\n\\nWhen you wrap a low-level error in a domain one, use `raise ... from` so the original traceback survives. Bare `raise NewError(...)` inside an `except` hides the root cause.\\n\\n```python\\ntry:\\n resp = await client.get(url)\\n resp.raise_for_status()\\nexcept httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:\\n raise QuotaExceededError(\\\"YouTube quota hit\\\") from e # ✓ keeps the cause\\n```\\n\\nTo deliberately suppress the context, use `from None` — and only when the cause is genuinely noise.\\n\\nThis is also how you keep storage details out of the API: the **repository** catches the driver error and raises a domain error, so the route never imports `sqlite3` or sees a driver exception.\\n\\n```python\\nimport sqlite3\\n\\ndef save_rule(self, rule: Rule) -> None:\\n try:\\n self._con.execute(\\\"INSERT INTO rules (id, pattern) VALUES (?, ?)\\\", (rule.id, rule.pattern))\\n except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:\\n raise DuplicateRuleError(rule.id) from e # domain error — a handler maps it to 409\\n```\\n\\n## else and finally\\n\\n`else` runs only when `try` didn't raise — put success logic there. `finally` always runs; prefer a **context manager** over manual try/finally.\\n\\n```python\\nwith open_connection(db_path) as conn: # closed on any exit path\\n conn.execute(...)\\n```\\n\\nWrite your own with `contextlib.contextmanager` or `__enter__/__exit__`; use `async with` for async resources.\\n\\n## Re-raise, don't return error sentinels\\n\\nReturning `None`/`-1`/`False` to signal failure forces every caller to remember to check, and the type checker can't help. Raise instead — the failure can't be silently ignored. (Return `X | None` only when \\\"not found\\\" is a *normal, expected* outcome, not an error.)\\n\\nIn async code, **never swallow `asyncio.CancelledError`** — re-raise it so shutdown and timeouts work (→ See `python-async`).\\n\\n## Mapping to HTTP\\n\\nIn FastAPI, register one exception handler per domain base class rather than try/except in every route (→ See `python-fastapi`):\\n\\n```python\\n@app.exception_handler(AuthRequiredError)\\nasync def _auth(_: Request, exc: AuthRequiredError):\\n return JSONResponse(status_code=401, content={\\\"detail\\\": str(exc)})\\n```\\n\\nNever leak a stack trace or internal message to a client — log the detail server-side, return a clean message.\\n\\n## Common mistakes\\n\\n| Mistake | Fix |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `except Exception: pass` | Catch the specific type; Bare `raise NewError(...)` inside an `except` hides the root cause.\n\n```python\ntry:\n resp = await client.get(url)\n resp.raise_for_status()\nexcept httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:\n raise QuotaExceededError(\"YouTube quota hit\") from e # ✓ keeps the cause\n```\n\nTo deliberately suppress the context, use `from None` — and only when the cause is genuinely noise.\n\nThis is also how you keep storage details out of the API: the **repository** catches the driver error and raises a domain error, so the route never imports `sqlite3` or sees a driver exception.\n\n```python\nimport sqlite3\n\ndef save_rule(self, rule: Rule) -> None:\n try:\n self._con.execute(\"INSERT INTO rules (id, pattern) VALUES (?, ?)\", (rule.id, rule.pattern))\n except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:\n raise DuplicateRuleError(rule.id) from e # domain error — a handler maps it to 409\n```\n\n## else and finally\n\n`else` runs only when `try` didn't raise — put success logic there. `finally` always runs; prefer a **context manager** over manual try/finally.\n\n```python\nwith open_connection(db_path) as conn: # closed on any exit path\n conn.execute(...)\n```\n\nWrite your own with `contextlib.contextmanager` or `__enter__/__exit__`; use `async with` for async resources.\n\n## Re-raise, don't return error sentinels\n\nReturning `None`/`-1`/`False` to signal failure forces every caller to remember to check, and the type checker can't help. Raise instead — the failure can't be silently ignored. (Return `X | None` only when \"not found\" is a *normal, expected* outcome, not an error.)\n\nIn async code, **never swallow `asyncio.CancelledError`** — re-raise it so shutdown and timeouts work (→ See `python-async`).\n\n## Mapping to HTTP\n\nIn FastAPI, register one exception handler per domain base class rather than try/except in every route (→ See `python-fastapi`):\n\n```python\n@app.exception_handler(AuthRequiredError)\nasync def _auth(_: Request, exc: AuthRequiredError):\n return JSONResponse(status_code=401, content={\"detail\": str(exc)})\n```\n\nNever leak a stack trace or internal message to a client — log the detail server-side, return a clean message.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `except Exception: pass` | Catch the specific type; if broad, `log.exception` then re-raise. |\n| Bare `raise FooError()` inside `except` | `raise FooError() from err` to preserve the cause. |\n| `except:` (bare) | Catches `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`/cancellation too — name the type. |\n| Manual try/finally for cleanup | Use a context manager (`with`). |\n| Returning `None`/`-1` for errors | Raise an exception; reserve `None` for expected absence. |\n| Swallowing `CancelledError` in async | Re-raise it. |\n| Leaking tracebacks to API clients | Log server-side; return a sanitized message. |\n| EAFP with broad `except` on a framework hierarchy | Prefer LBYL guard or narrow catch; wrap at the boundary into a domain exception. |\n\n**Diagnose:** 1- `ruff check` (bugbear `B`) — flags overly broad `except` and `raise` without `from` 2- read the full traceback (don't truncate) — the chained `from` cause usually names the real failure.\n\n## References\n\n- [Errors and Exceptions — tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html)\n- [Built-in Exceptions](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html)\n- [Glossary — EAFP / LBYL](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html)\n- [Alexis King — Parse, don't validate](https://lexi-lambda.github.io/blog/2019/11/05/parse-don-t-validate/)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-error-handling\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"

        "<skill_content name=\"python-error-handling\">\n# Skill: python-error-handling\n\n> Pair with `python-common-practice`, `python-fastapi` (HTTP mapping), `python-async` (CancelledError), and `python-observability` (logging errors) as relevant.\n\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats exceptions as part of the API. You catch what you can handle and let the rest propagate to someone who can.\n\n# Error Handling\n\nPython prefers **EAFP** (\"easier to ask forgiveness than permission\") — try the operation and handle the exception rather than pre-checking. Pre-checks race with reality; the exception is the truth.\n\n```python\n# ✓ EAFP — one atomic attempt\ntry:\n return cache[key]\nexcept KeyError:\n return load(key)\n\n# ✗ LBYL — racy for I/O; fine when a simple guard avoids broad catching\nif key in cache:\n return cache[key]\n```\n\n**EAFP is a convention, not a universal rule.** Broad catches can hide failures from both humans and agents. Prefer EAFP where the exception type is known and the catch is narrow; inspect the framework's actual error behavior rather than guessing at its hierarchy. Use explicit checks where they express the contract more clearly, while accounting for race conditions between checking and acting.\n\n## Catch narrowly\n\nCatch the **specific** exception you can handle. A bare `except:` or `except Exception:` swallows bugs, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and (in async) cancellation — turning a crash you'd fix into silent wrong behavior.\n\n```python\n# ✗ Bad — hides programming errors and makes debugging impossible\ntry:\n sync_playlist(p)\nexcept Exception:\n pass\n\n# ✓ Good — handle the failures you expect; let the rest surface\ntry:\n sync_playlist(p)\nexcept (httpx.HTTPError, TimeoutError) as e:\n log.warning(\"sync failed for %s: %s\", p.id, e)\n metrics.errors_total.inc()\n```\n\nIf you must catch broadly (a top-level worker loop that must not die), log with `log.exception(...)` to capture the traceback, then continue or re-raise — never `pass`.\n\n## Agent navigability — narrow exception surfaces\n\nPrefer narrow exception surfaces: agents catching from broad hierarchies must guess error object shapes — a predictable interface failure, not a model failure.\n\n**Framework guidance — catch the specific exception, not the family:**\n\n| Framework | Broad (avoid) | Narrow (prefer) |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `requests` / `httpx` | `requests.exceptions.RequestException` | `httpx.TimeoutException`, `httpx.HTTPStatusError` |\n| `django` ORM | `django.core.exceptions.ObjectDoesNotExist` | `MyModel.DoesNotExist` |\n| SQLAlchemy | `sqlalchemy.exc.SQLAlchemyError` | `sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError`, `sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError` |\n\nWrap framework exceptions at the boundary into domain exceptions. This collapses the broad hierarchy into a predictable, narrow surface for all downstream code.\n\n## Custom exceptions — a hierarchy with a common base\n\nGive your package one base exception; specific errors subclass it. Callers can then catch the whole family or a specific case. This is what lets a FastAPI handler map *all* your domain errors in one place.\n\n```python\nclass SortarrError(Exception):\n \"\"\"Base for all sortarr domain errors.\"\"\"\n\nclass AuthRequiredError(SortarrError): ...\nclass QuotaExceededError(SortarrError): ...\n```\n\nSubclass the most specific stdlib type when it fits (`ValueError`, `LookupError`); invent a new hierarchy only for domain concepts the stdlib doesn't model.\n\n## Chain exceptions — preserve the cause\n\nWhen you wrap a low-level error in a domain one, use `raise ... from` so the original traceback survives. Bare `raise NewError(...)` inside an `except` hides the root cause.\n\n```python\ntry:\n resp = await client.get(url)\n resp.raise_for_status()\nexcept httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:\n raise QuotaExceededError(\"YouTube quota hit\") from e # ✓ keeps the cause\n```\n\nTo deliberately suppress the context, use `from None` — and only when the cause is genuinely noise.\n\nThis is also how you keep storage details out of the API: the **repository** catches the driver error and raises a domain error, so the route never imports `sqlite3` or sees a driver exception.\n\n```python\nimport sqlite3\n\ndef save_rule(self, rule: Rule) -> None:\n try:\n self._con.execute(\"INSERT INTO rules (id, pattern) VALUES (?, ?)\", (rule.id, rule.pattern))\n except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:\n raise DuplicateRuleError(rule.id) from e # domain error — a handler maps it to 409\n```\n\n## else and finally\n\n`else` runs only when `try` didn't raise — put success logic there. `finally` always runs; prefer a **context manager** over manual try/finally.\n\n```python\nwith open_connection(db_path) as conn: # closed on any exit path\n conn.execute(...)\n```\n\nWrite your own with `contextlib.contextmanager` or `__enter__/__exit__`; use `async with` for async resources.\n\n## Re-raise, don't return error sentinels\n\nReturning `None`/`-1`/`False` to signal failure forces every caller to remember to check, and the type checker can't help. Raise instead — the failure can't be silently ignored. (Return `X | None` only when \"not found\" is a *normal, expected* outcome, not an error.)\n\nIn async code, **never swallow `asyncio.CancelledError`** — re-raise it so shutdown and timeouts work (→ See `python-async`).\n\n## Mapping to HTTP\n\nIn FastAPI, register one exception handler per domain base class rather than try/except in every route (→ See `python-fastapi`):\n\n```python\n@app.exception_handler(AuthRequiredError)\nasync def _auth(_: Request, exc: AuthRequiredError):\n return JSONResponse(status_code=401, content={\"detail\": str(exc)})\n```\n\nNever leak a stack trace or internal message to a client — log the detail server-side, return a clean message.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `except Exception: pass` | Catch the specific type; if broad, `log.exception` then re-raise. |\n| Bare `raise FooError()` inside `except` | `raise FooError() from err` to preserve the cause. |\n| `except:` (bare) | Catches `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`/cancellation too — name the type. |\n| Manual try/finally for cleanup | Use a context manager (`with`). |\n| Returning `None`/`-1` for errors | Raise an exception; reserve `None` for expected absence. |\n| Swallowing `CancelledError` in async | Re-raise it. |\n| Leaking tracebacks to API clients | Log server-side; return a sanitized message. |\n| EAFP with broad `except` on a framework hierarchy | Prefer LBYL guard or narrow catch; wrap at the boundary into a domain exception. |\n\n**Diagnose:** 1- `ruff check` (bugbear `B`) — flags overly broad `except` and `raise` without `from` 2- read the full traceback (don't truncate) — the chained `from` cause usually names the real failure.\n\n## References\n\n- [Errors and Exceptions — tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html)\n- [Built-in Exceptions](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html)\n- [Glossary — EAFP / LBYL](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html)\n- [Alexis King — Parse, don't validate](https://lexi-lambda.github.io/blog/2019/11/05/parse-don-t-validate/)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-error-handling\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"

      "{\"type\":\"step_start\",\"timestamp\":1793301235668,\"sessionID\":\"ses_e76eab9c7ffe1cv3xPCTnNCbGR\",\"part\":{\"id\":\"prt_1891547d4001fRFP1irla13Oby\",\"sessionID\":\"ses_e76eab9c7ffe1cv3xPCTnNCbGR\",\"messageID\":\"msg_1891547ba001qYA2jsBmoKzBuV\",\"type\":\"step-start\"}}\n{\"type\":\"tool_use\",\"timestamp\":1793301235685,\"sessionID\":\"ses_e76eab9c7ffe1cv3xPCTnNCbGR\",\"part\":{\"partID\":\"prt_1891547d7001TiO1qBumzHTBHo\",\"sessionID\":\"ses_e76eab9c7ffe1cv3xPCTnNCbGR\",\"messageID\":\"msg_1891547ba001qYA2jsBmoKzBuV\",\"type\":\"tool\",\"id\":\"fixture-skill-call\",\"tool\":\"skill\",\"state\":{\"status\":\"completed\",\"input\":{\"id\":\"python-error-handling\"},\"output\":\"<skill_content name=\\\"python-error-handling\\\">\\n# Skill: python-error-handling\\n\\n> Pair with `python-common-practice`, `python-fastapi` (HTTP mapping), `python-async` (CancelledError), and `python-observability` (logging errors) as relevant.\\n\\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats exceptions as part of the API. You catch what you can handle and let the rest propagate to someone who can.\\n\\n# Error Handling\\n\\nPython prefers **EAFP** (\\\"easier to ask forgiveness than permission\\\") — try the operation and handle the exception rather than pre-checking. Pre-checks race with reality; the exception is the truth.\\n\\n```python\\n# ✓ EAFP — one atomic attempt\\ntry:\\n return cache[key]\\nexcept KeyError:\\n return load(key)\\n\\n# ✗ LBYL — racy for I/O; fine when a simple guard avoids broad catching\\nif key in cache:\\n return cache[key]\\n```\\n\\n**EAFP is a convention, not a universal rule.** Broad catches can hide failures from both humans and agents. Prefer EAFP where the exception type is known and the catch is narrow; inspect the framework's actual error behavior rather than guessing at its hierarchy. Use explicit checks where they express the contract more clearly, while accounting for race conditions between checking and acting.\\n\\n## Catch narrowly\\n\\nCatch the **specific** exception you can handle. A bare `except:` or `except Exception:` swallows bugs, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and (in async) cancellation — turning a crash you'd fix into silent wrong behavior.\\n\\n```python\\n# ✗ Bad — hides programming errors and makes debugging impossible\\ntry:\\n sync_playlist(p)\\nexcept Exception:\\n pass\\n\\n# ✓ Good — handle the failures you expect; let the rest surface\\ntry:\\n sync_playlist(p)\\nexcept (httpx.HTTPError, TimeoutError) as e:\\n log.warning(\\\"sync failed for %s: %s\\\", p.id, e)\\n metrics.errors_total.inc()\\n```\\n\\nIf you must catch broadly (a top-level worker loop that must not die), log with `log.exception(...)` to capture the traceback, then continue or re-raise — never `pass`.\\n\\n## Agent navigability — narrow exception surfaces\\n\\nPrefer narrow exception surfaces: agents catching from broad hierarchies must guess error object shapes — a predictable interface failure, not a model failure.\\n\\n**Framework guidance — catch the specific exception, not the family:**\\n\\n| Framework | Broad (avoid) | Narrow (prefer) |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| `requests` / `httpx` | `requests.exceptions.RequestException` | `httpx.TimeoutException`, `httpx.HTTPStatusError` |\\n| `django` ORM | `django.core.exceptions.ObjectDoesNotExist` | `MyModel.DoesNotExist` |\\n| SQLAlchemy | `sqlalchemy.exc.SQLAlchemyError` | `sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError`, `sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError` |\\n\\nWrap framework exceptions at the boundary into domain exceptions. This collapses the broad hierarchy into a predictable, narrow surface for all downstream code.\\n\\n## Custom exceptions — a hierarchy with a common base\\n\\nGive your package one base exception; specific errors subclass it. Callers can then catch the whole family or a specific case. This is what lets a FastAPI handler map *all* your domain errors in one place.\\n\\n```python\\nclass SortarrError(Exception):\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Base for all sortarr domain errors.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nclass AuthRequiredError(SortarrError): ...\\nclass QuotaExceededError(SortarrError): ...\\n```\\n\\nSubclass the most specific stdlib type when it fits (`ValueError`, `LookupError`); invent a new hierarchy only for domain concepts the stdlib doesn't model.\\n\\n## Chain exceptions — preserve the cause\\n\\nWhen you wrap a low-level error in a domain one, use `raise ... from` so the original traceback survives. Bare `raise NewError(...)` inside an `except` hides the root cause.\\n\\n```python\\ntry:\\n resp = await client.get(url)\\n resp.raise_for_status()\\nexcept httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:\\n raise QuotaExceededError(\\\"YouTube quota hit\\\") from e # ✓ keeps the cause\\n```\\n\\nTo deliberately suppress the context, use `from None` — and only when the cause is genuinely noise.\\n\\nThis is also how you keep storage details out of the API: the **repository** catches the driver error and raises a domain error, so the route never imports `sqlite3` or sees a driver exception.\\n\\n```python\\nimport sqlite3\\n\\ndef save_rule(self, rule: Rule) -> None:\\n try:\\n self._con.execute(\\\"INSERT INTO rules (id, pattern) VALUES (?, ?)\\\", (rule.id, rule.pattern))\\n except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:\\n raise DuplicateRuleError(rule.id) from e # domain error — a handler maps it to 409\\n```\\n\\n## else and finally\\n\\n`else` runs only when `try` didn't raise — put success logic there. `finally` always runs; prefer a **context manager** over manual try/finally.\\n\\n```python\\nwith open_connection(db_path) as conn: # closed on any exit path\\n conn.execute(...)\\n```\\n\\nWrite your own with `contextlib.contextmanager` or `__enter__/__exit__`; use `async with` for async resources.\\n\\n## Re-raise, don't return error sentinels\\n\\nReturning `None`/`-1`/`False` to signal failure forces every caller to remember to check, and the type checker can't help. Raise instead — the failure can't be silently ignored. (Return `X | None` only when \\\"not found\\\" is a *normal, expected* outcome, not an error.)\\n\\nIn async code, **never swallow `asyncio.CancelledError`** — re-raise it so shutdown and timeouts work (→ See `python-async`).\\n\\n## Mapping to HTTP\\n\\nIn FastAPI, register one exception handler per domain base class rather than try/except in every route (→ See `python-fastapi`):\\n\\n```python\\n@app.exception_handler(AuthRequiredError)\\nasync def _auth(_: Request, exc: AuthRequiredError):\\n return JSONResponse(status_code=401, content={\\\"detail\\\": str(exc)})\\n```\\n\\nNever leak a stack trace or internal message to a client — log the detail server-side, return a clean message.\\n\\n## Common mistakes\\n\\n| Mistake | Fix |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `except Exception: pass` | Catch the specific type; if broad, `log.exception` then re-raise. |\\n| Bare `raise FooError()` inside `except` | `raise FooError() from err` to preserve the cause. |\\n| `except:` (bare) | Catches `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`/cancellation too — name the type. |\\n| Manual try/finally for cleanup | Use a context manager (`with`). |\\n| Returning `None`/`-1` for errors | Raise an exception; reserve `None` for expected absence. |\\n| Swallowing `CancelledError` in async | Re-raise it. |\\n| Leaking tracebacks to API clients | Log server-side; return a sanitized message. |\\n| EAFP with broad `except` on a framework hierarchy | Prefer LBYL guard or narrow catch;
